purpose: Short preliminary form-selection and complexity check, not a legal eligibility certification or filing approval.

resultPolicy.next: Advance to the next question. If every response is next, use the final title You can continue.
resultPolicy.stop: The stated role or purpose does not match this form; explain stopReason without saying the person is ineligible for immigration benefits.
resultPolicy.review: Explain reviewReason and offer individual review; do not label the person ineligible.
resultPolicy.continueDescription: Your answers fit this preliminary preparation path. The complete USCIS requirements, current instructions and your documents still need to be checked.

verificationNotes: USCIS HTML/browser-reader requests returned 403. Official PDF URLs were downloaded successfully and their instruction text was inspected directly.
Each pdfUrl contains an official PDF with interactive Widget annotations; download SHA-256 and widget count are recorded. No PDF was modified.
Downloaded form/instruction editions are recorded as source evidence; a filing workflow must check the USCIS landing page for the currently accepted edition and any new alerts.
Military, K-3, waiver, late-filing and other special paths are intentionally sent to review rather than forced through ordinary rules.

forms.scope: Preliminary routing for ordinary five-year and marriage-based three-year naturalization. Military service, VAWA and other special routes require review rather than rejection.
sourceSections: Good moral character and military service

pdfVerification.method: Downloaded from the official USCIS URL; PDF signature, form title and interactive Widget annotations inspected with pdfplumber.

questions.text: Are you already a U.S. citizen?
questions.help: A person who already acquired citizenship generally needs proof of citizenship, not naturalization.
questions.stopReason: N-400 applies for naturalization. Explore the appropriate proof-of-citizenship document instead.

questions.text: Are you using the usual five-year residence route or the three-year route as the spouse of a U.S. citizen?
questions.help: Military service, VAWA, qualifying employment abroad and other special provisions have different rules.
questions.reviewReason: A special naturalization route may apply. Review its requirements; this is not a finding that you are ineligible.

questions.text: Are you at least 18 and a lawful permanent resident?
questions.help: This question applies to the ordinary routes above. Some military provisions have different age or residence rules.
questions.reviewReason: Age, residence status or a possible special route needs review.

questions.text: Have you checked that you meet the residence, physical-presence and filing-date rules for your route?
questions.help: The usual routes generally require five years with 30 months of physical presence, or three years with 18 months for a qualifying U.S.-citizen spouse; three-month state/district residence also matters. Limited 90-day early filing does not waive other requirements.
questions.reviewReason: Review the applicable residence period, travel history, marriage requirements and earliest filing date before continuing.

questions.text: Are you prepared to meet the English and civics requirements, or have you identified an applicable exception?
questions.help: Age/residence exceptions, disability exceptions and accommodations require their own checks; needing one does not make you ineligible.
questions.reviewReason: Review the testing rules and any exception or accommodation that may apply.

questions.text: Is your case free of issues that need individual review, such as arrests, tax or support problems, removal proceedings, citizenship claims or long absences?
questions.help: A past issue does not automatically prevent naturalization. Its facts and timing matter.
questions.reviewReason: An attorney or accredited representative should review the relevant history before a filing decision.

forms.scope: Renewal or replacement of an existing permanent resident card. This screen does not determine whether permanent resident status remains valid.
sourceSections: Reason for application and required evidence

pdfVerification.method: Downloaded from the official USCIS URL; PDF signature, form title and interactive Widget annotations inspected with pdfplumber.

questions.text: Are you already a lawful permanent resident, including a conditional or commuter resident?
questions.help: I-90 replaces an existing resident card; it does not apply for a first green card.
questions.stopReason: I-90 is for people who already have permanent resident status.

questions.text: Do you need to renew, replace or correct your existing green card?
questions.help: Examples include a lost, stolen, damaged or incorrect card, a qualifying renewal, or another I-90 reason listed in the instructions.
questions.stopReason: I-90 is for an existing green-card document, not another immigration benefit.

questions.text: Are you trying to remove conditions on a two-year green card?
questions.help: Marriage-based conditions normally use I-751; investment-based conditions use I-829.
questions.stopReason: Use the removal-of-conditions process rather than I-90 for this purpose.

questions.text: Is your card a two-year conditional card that has expired or will expire within 90 days?
questions.help: USCIS instructions exclude I-90 replacement of such a card for any reason. Review the proper evidence-of-status or removal-of-conditions process.
questions.reviewReason: The conditional-card timing needs a different process or individual review; do not treat I-90 as a renewal of conditional residence.

questions.text: Are you outside the U.S. and missing the documents needed to board your return trip?
questions.help: Replacing a card and obtaining carrier documentation are different processes.
questions.reviewReason: Review travel and carrier-documentation requirements before relying on I-90 for return travel.

forms.scope: Preliminary family-petition routing. Approval of I-130 does not itself grant status or decide green-card eligibility.
sourceSections: Who may file and non-citizen nationals

pdfVerification.method: Downloaded from the official USCIS URL; PDF signature, form title and interactive Widget annotations inspected with pdfplumber.

questions.text: Is the petitioner a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident or non-citizen U.S. national?
questions.help: Answer about the family member signing the petition, not the intending immigrant.
questions.stopReason: The I-130 petitioner must hold one of these qualifying statuses.

questions.text: Is the beneficiary your spouse, child, son or daughter, parent, brother or sister?
questions.help: Other family relationships, such as a cousin or grandparent, do not create their own I-130 category.
questions.stopReason: The stated relationship does not match an I-130 family category.

questions.text: Does your status and age support the family category you selected?
questions.help: Citizens may petition for spouses and children; petitioning for a parent or sibling requires a citizen age 21 or older. Permanent residents and non-citizen nationals may petition for spouses and unmarried children or adult sons/daughters.
questions.reviewReason: Check the petitioner status, age and beneficiary marital status before choosing a family category.

questions.text: Does this case involve adoption, a step-relationship, a proxy marriage or marriage during removal proceedings?
questions.help: These relationships have additional rules or exceptions.
questions.reviewReason: Review the relationship-specific requirements; the relationship is not automatically disqualified.

questions.text: Are there prior marriage-based immigration issues, a marriage-fraud finding or a potentially relevant criminal history?
questions.help: Special restrictions and exceptions can depend on the exact facts.
questions.reviewReason: Individual review is needed before continuing with this family petition.

forms.scope: Preliminary adjustment-of-status routing for a person physically in the U.S. It does not evaluate admissibility, current visa availability or every statutory exception.
sourceSections: Who may file, bars and exceptions
When to file and category-specific requirements

pdfVerification.method: Downloaded from the official USCIS URL; PDF signature, form title and interactive Widget annotations inspected with pdfplumber.

questions.text: Are you physically present in the United States?
questions.help: I-485 requests adjustment of status from within the U.S.
questions.stopReason: I-485 is filed by a person physically in the U.S.; review the immigrant-visa process for a person abroad.

questions.text: Are you applying for permanent residence rather than only replacing or renewing a green card?
questions.help: Card replacement usually uses I-90; removing conditions has a separate process.
questions.stopReason: Choose the card-replacement or removal-of-conditions process if that is your only request.

questions.text: Have you identified a specific adjustment category for yourself or as a qualifying derivative?
questions.help: Family, employment, refugee/asylee and other categories have different rules. A relative in the U.S. alone does not establish a filing basis.
questions.reviewReason: Identify and review the legal filing basis before starting I-485.

questions.text: Have you confirmed that your category permits filing now, including any visa-availability requirement?
questions.help: Some categories permit concurrent filing; others require an approved petition, an available visa number or a category-specific waiting period.
questions.reviewReason: Review the current category and filing-date rules. This check does not calculate visa availability.

questions.text: Were you inspected and admitted or paroled at your most recent entry?
questions.help: A No answer needs review: special categories and provisions such as INA 245(i) may have different rules.
questions.reviewReason: Review the entry history and any applicable exception; this answer does not automatically rule out adjustment.

questions.text: Is your case free of issues such as immigration-court proceedings, prior removal, unauthorized work, status violations, arrests or misrepresentation?
questions.help: Some issues have exceptions or waivers; others affect who has authority to decide the case.
questions.reviewReason: Individual review is needed for possible bars, waivers, exceptions or court jurisdiction.

forms.scope: Preliminary routing for employment authorization or an EAD. An identified eligibility category and its current filing rules are required; this screen does not grant work authorization.

pdfVerification.method: Downloaded from the official USCIS URL; PDF signature, form title and interactive Widget annotations inspected with pdfplumber.

questions.text: Are you requesting an initial, renewed or replacement Employment Authorization Document (EAD)?
questions.help: An EAD is a work-authorization card; I-765 does not itself request a green card.
questions.stopReason: I-765 is for employment authorization or an EAD, not another immigration document.

questions.text: Are you a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident, including a conditional resident?
questions.help: Citizens and permanent residents do not use I-765 to document their ordinary right to work.
questions.stopReason: Use your appropriate citizenship or permanent-resident evidence of work authorization rather than I-765.

questions.text: Are you currently in the United States?
questions.help: Some processing situations require a closer review of the category and location.
questions.reviewReason: Review the filing category and location rules before choosing I-765.

questions.text: Have you identified your exact I-765 eligibility category in the current USCIS instructions?
questions.help: The category code in Part 2, Item 27 depends on the underlying status or benefit. Employer-specific work authorization alone is not an I-765 category.
questions.reviewReason: Review the underlying status and category code; a desire to work alone is not a filing basis.

questions.text: Can you document the status, pending application or other basis required for that category?
questions.help: A pending benefit and an approved benefit can use different categories.
questions.reviewReason: Confirm the underlying basis and required documents before starting the EAD request.

questions.text: Have you checked the filing window and category-specific requirements for this initial, renewal or replacement request?
questions.help: Student employment, pending asylum, DACA and other categories have distinct timing and evidence rules.
questions.reviewReason: Review the exact category instructions and current USCIS guidance before continuing.

forms.scope: Preliminary routing for removal of marriage-based conditions. Waivers, children filing separately and late filings are sent for review rather than marked ineligible.
sourceSections: Who may file, children and individual/waiver routes

pdfVerification.method: Downloaded from the official USCIS URL; PDF signature, form title and interactive Widget annotations inspected with pdfplumber.

questions.text: Did you obtain conditional residence through your marriage or your parent’s marriage?
questions.help: Investment-based conditional residence uses a different petition.
questions.stopReason: I-751 is for marriage-based conditional residence, including qualifying children.

questions.text: Are you asking to remove the conditions on that residence?
questions.help: Replacing a lost card is different from removing conditions.
questions.stopReason: I-751 is the removal-of-conditions petition; choose the document-replacement process if that is your only need.

questions.text: Is this a routine joint petition with the spouse through whom conditional residence was obtained?
questions.help: Divorce, a spouse’s death, battery or extreme cruelty, hardship and children filing separately may allow other routes.
questions.reviewReason: Review an individual filing or waiver route. A spouse’s unwillingness or inability to join is not an automatic denial.

questions.text: Will you file during the 90 days immediately before conditional residence expires?
questions.help: This timing question applies to a routine joint filing. Waivers and justified late filings have different rules.
questions.reviewReason: Review the correct filing date or grounds for a late-filing request; do not assume there is no available route.

questions.text: Is the case free of immigration-court proceedings or other circumstances that need individual review?
questions.help: A pending removal case or other complication can affect how to proceed.
questions.reviewReason: Review the case history and procedure before continuing.

forms.scope: Preliminary K-1 fiancé(e) petition routing, with K-3 spouse petitions expressly sent for review. It does not screen all IMBRA, criminal-history or waiver rules.
sourceSections: K-1 and K-3 purposes and who may file

pdfVerification.method: Downloaded from the official USCIS URL; PDF signature, form title and interactive Widget annotations inspected with pdfplumber.

questions.text: Is the petitioner a U.S. citizen?
questions.help: Answer about the person signing the petition, not the beneficiary.
questions.stopReason: I-129F is filed by a U.S. citizen petitioner.

questions.text: Is this for a fiancé(e) seeking K-1 status or a spouse seeking K-3 status?
questions.help: Both uses appear in the USCIS I-129F instructions.
questions.stopReason: This request does not match the K-1 or K-3 purpose of I-129F.

questions.text: Are you petitioning for a spouse under the K-3 route?
questions.help: The K-3 route involves a spouse and a filed or concurrently filing I-130; it does not use the K-1 unmarried-fiancé requirements.
questions.reviewReason: Review the K-3 spouse route and the I-130 filing. Being married is not a reason to reject this I-129F use.

questions.text: Are you both legally free to marry and intending to marry within 90 days after the fiancé(e)’s U.S. admission?
questions.help: This question applies only to the K-1 fiancé(e) route.
questions.reviewReason: Review the K-1 marriage requirements and timing before continuing.

questions.text: Have you met in person during the two years immediately before filing?
questions.help: Limited exceptions exist for extreme hardship to the petitioner or qualifying long-established customs.
questions.reviewReason: Review whether a meeting exception applies; a No answer is not an automatic finding of ineligibility.

questions.text: Is the case free of prior K-1 filings or relevant criminal-history issues requiring extra review?
questions.help: Multiple-filing limits, disclosure duties and possible waivers may apply.
questions.reviewReason: Review prior petitions, criminal-history disclosures and any waiver requirements.

forms.scope: Preliminary financial-sponsor routing. This screen does not compute household income, assess asset sufficiency or decide an exemption from sponsorship.
sourceSections: Household income, assets and joint sponsors

pdfVerification.method: Downloaded from the official USCIS URL; PDF signature, form title and interactive Widget annotations inspected with pdfplumber.

questions.text: Are you preparing this affidavit for the person who will sign as a financial sponsor?
questions.help: Answer the remaining questions about that sponsor. Petitioning, joint and substitute sponsors may have distinct requirements.
questions.stopReason: I-864 is completed and signed by a qualifying financial sponsor.

questions.text: Is the signing sponsor at least 18 and a U.S. citizen, U.S. national or lawful permanent resident?
questions.help: These are sponsor requirements, separate from the intending immigrant’s eligibility.
questions.stopReason: The signing I-864 sponsor must meet the age and qualifying-status requirements.

questions.text: Have you confirmed that the intending immigrant needs an I-864 for this case?
questions.help: Most family cases and some employment cases require it, but certain immigrants are exempt.
questions.reviewReason: Review whether I-864 is required, an exemption applies or another support form is appropriate.

questions.text: Can the sponsor document a U.S. domicile or a permitted way to establish it by the required time?
questions.help: Living abroad does not automatically fail this requirement; retained domicile, qualifying employment and reestablishing domicile need evidence.
questions.reviewReason: Review domicile and any permitted exception or plan to reestablish it.

questions.text: Can the sponsor document sufficient qualifying income or assets for the household-size requirement?
questions.help: The general standard is 125% of the applicable poverty guideline; qualifying active-duty sponsors of a spouse or child may use 100%. Household members or a joint sponsor may help under separate rules.
questions.reviewReason: Review income, assets, household size and possible additional sponsorship; low individual income is not an automatic end to the case.

questions.text: Is this a routine petitioning-sponsor case without a joint sponsor, substitute sponsor, household-member contract or exemption issue?
questions.help: These situations may be permitted, but require more detailed checks.
questions.reviewReason: Review the applicable additional sponsor, I-864A or exemption requirements.
